Fix \(p\in(1,2)\cup(2,\infty)\) and put \(q=p/(p-1)\). A matrix weight is a measurable function \(W:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C^{2\times2}\) whose entries are locally integrable and whose values are Hermitian positive definite almost everywhere. Matrix powers are defined by spectral calculus. Write \(|v|\) for the Euclidean norm on \(\mathbb C^2\) and \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) for its induced matrix operator norm.

Define
\[
[W]_{A_p}=\sup_I\frac1{|I|}\int_I
\Big(\frac1{|I|}\int_I
\|W(x)^{1/p}W(y)^{-1/p}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^q\,dy\Big)^{p-1}\,dx,
\]
where the supremum runs over all intervals \(I\subset\mathbb R\) of positive finite length and all integrals use Lebesgue measure. For measurable \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C^2\), set
\[
\|f\|_{L^p(W)}=\Big(\int_{\mathbb R}|W(x)^{1/p}f(x)|^p\,dx\Big)^{1/p}.
\]
The Hilbert transform acts componentwise on smooth compactly supported vector-valued functions by
\[
Hf(x)=\frac1\pi\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\int_{|x-y|>\varepsilon}\frac{f(y)}{x-y}\,dy.
\]
Let \(\beta(p)\) be the infimum of all real \(\gamma\ge0\) for which there exists a finite constant \(C_{p,\gamma}\), independent of \(W\) and \(f\), such that
\[
\|Hf\|_{L^p(W)}\le C_{p,\gamma}[W]_{A_p}^{\gamma}\|f\|_{L^p(W)}
\]
for every matrix weight \(W\) with \([W]_{A_p}<\infty\) and every smooth compactly supported \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C^2\). What is the exact formula for \(\beta(p)\)?

assert sp.simplify((q-1)*(p-1)-1) == 0

characteristic_on_01 = 1/eps * ((p-1)/(p-eps))**(p-1)

# The change of variables s=-eps log x removes the singular measure.
mp.mp.dps = 35
for power in [mp.mpf('1.5'), mp.mpf('3')]:
    limit = mp.gamma(power+1)**(1/power)/mp.pi
    print('p =', power, 'asymptotic scaled ratio =', mp.nstr(limit, 12))
    for e in [mp.mpf('.2'), mp.mpf('.1'), mp.mpf('.05')]:
        def integrand(s):

                return mp.mpf(0)  # endpoint value does not affect integral
            term = s + e*mp.log(-mp.expm1(-s/e))

        val = mp.quad(integrand, [0, e*mp.log(2), 1, 4, mp.inf])
        scaled_ratio = val**(1/power)/mp.pi

### The obstruction \(\gamma\geq1\)

Let \(0<\varepsilon\leq\tfrac12\) and
\[
v_\varepsilon(x)=|x|^{-1+\varepsilon}.
\]
For every \(r>1\),
\[
[v_\varepsilon]_{A_r}\leq \frac2\varepsilon.
\]
Indeed, on an interval \((a,b)\subset(0,\infty)\), if \(a\geq b/2\), comparison with the endpoint values bounds the \(A_r\) expression by \(2^{1-\varepsilon}\). If \(a<b/2\), use
\[
\frac1{b-a}\int_a^b v_\varepsilon
\leq \frac{2b^{-1+\varepsilon}}{\varepsilon},
\qquad
\frac1{b-a}\int_a^b v_\varepsilon^{-1/(r-1)}
\leq b^{(1-\varepsilon)/(r-1)}.
\]
Intervals in the negative half-line follow by symmetry. For an interval \((-a,b)\) crossing zero, put \(\ell=a+b\) and use
\[
a^\varepsilon+b^\varepsilon\leq2^{1-\varepsilon}\ell^\varepsilon,
\qquad
|x|^{(1-\varepsilon)/(r-1)}
\leq\ell^{(1-\varepsilon)/(r-1)}.
\]

Now take \(f=\mathbf1_{(0,1)}\). Its Hilbert transform is
\[
Hf(x)=\frac1\pi\log\left|\frac{x}{x-1}\right|,
\qquad
\|f\|_{L^p(v_\varepsilon)}^p=\frac1\varepsilon.
\]
Writing \(x=e^{-t}\), and restricting to \(1/\varepsilon\leq t\leq2/\varepsilon\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|Hf\|_{L^p(v_\varepsilon)}^p
&\geq \frac1{(2\pi)^p}
\int_{1/\varepsilon}^{2/\varepsilon}t^pe^{-\varepsilon t}\,dt\\
&\geq \frac{e^{-2}}{(2\pi)^p}\varepsilon^{-p-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently the operator-norm ratio is at least \(c_p/\varepsilon\), whereas the characteristic is at most \(2/\varepsilon\). Any exponent in the proposed inequality must therefore satisfy \(\gamma\geq1\).

### The obstruction \(\gamma\geq1/(p-1)\)

Set
\[
w_\varepsilon(x)=|x|^{(p-1)(1-\varepsilon)},
\qquad
g_\varepsilon(x)=x^{-1+\varepsilon}\mathbf1_{(0,1)}(x).
\]
Scalar duality of the characteristics gives
\[
[w_\varepsilon]_{A_p}
=[v_\varepsilon]_{A_q}^{p-1}
\leq(2/\varepsilon)^{p-1}.
\]
Also,
\[
\|g_\varepsilon\|_{L^p(w_\varepsilon)}^p=\frac1\varepsilon.
\]
For \(0<t<1\), there is no principal-value issue at \(x=-t\), and
\[
|Hg_\varepsilon(-t)|
=\frac1\pi\int_0^1\frac{y^{-1+\varepsilon}}{t+y}\,dy
\geq\frac{t^{-1+\varepsilon}}{2\pi\varepsilon}.
\]
Thus
\[
\|Hg_\varepsilon\|_{L^p(w_\varepsilon)}^p
\geq (2\pi\varepsilon)^{-p}\varepsilon^{-1}.
\]
The norm ratio is at least \((2\pi\varepsilon)^{-1}\), forcing
\((p-1)\gamma\geq1\).
